LESSON: WATER

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: RESOURCES IN OUR ENVIRONMENT Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sugges
Topic 3.1: Water
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Water, part of RESOURCES IN OUR ENVIRONMENT Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sugges in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can you keep water clean and safe?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign words related to water, name ways in which water can be contaminated in the environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Water in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. carry out activities to make water clean,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Water in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. conserve water at home and school as scarce resource,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Water in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

A. value the importance of clean and safe water for healthy living.. ●

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Water in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. sign words related to water, name ways in which water can be contaminated in the environment,

   Water helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. carry out activities to make water clean,

   Water helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. conserve water at home and school as scarce resource,

   Water helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. value the importance of clean and safe water for healthy living.. ●

   Water helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Water together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: team spirit as learners work collaboratively when making a water filter from locally available materials.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Life skills: learners enhance unity and cooperation instead of competition as they make improvised filters from locally available

materials.

● Health promotion issues: Communicable and non-communicable disease prevention: as learners discuss ways of making water safe for

drinking.

Link to other learning areas

Learners relate to creative skills learnt in Creative Activities as they make improvised filters from locally available materials.

Suggested Learning Resources:

approved textbooks, water, sieves, soil, charcoal, pictures, digital devices, white piece of cloth, plastic containers,
